content_of_post_to_comment: Just read about how writers like Emily Dickinson and Jane Austen experienced very little of what they actually wrote. Bram Stoker never visited Eastern Europe. Herman Melville never set foot on Nantucket. Cormac McCarthy may have famously walked the same trail as the Glanton Gang, but he could barely ride a horse. Instead, these writers had their libraries, and they watched those around them, and they listened. The more I write, the more I’m persuaded of the value of simply being curious and paying attention to what’s around us.
